title: More students, measured first: no planted student earns an exam, the generator's layouts named the truths, tuning gets its evidence
request: The owner's step 5: 'More students (toward 100): first the 16 points whose answers can be planted, then the workflow points with recorded steps'; then 'Both parts': reuse the split and cleaning students on the weak choices, measure the rule on planted files for the other four, a student only where the rule errs.
spec: docs/guides/STUDENTS_100_PLAN.md S3: a student only where it has labelled examples and a rule to beat; decision_gate_v1 unchanged; a sealed set read once.
plan: Measure today's rule on planted tables before building anything.
Map an existing student's answer where its skill already covers a weak choice.
Homework and exam on fresh seeds, states written by production's own capture.
Check each mapped student on dev with the gate's own function; fix the exam's scope before the read.

decisions.decision: No new student for nine of the sixteen planted points.
decisions.why: Settings, a definition, choices DCLab does not make, a choice with no rule by design, or a truth only people hold: a student could only copy the rule.

decisions.decision: Map the split student onto groups and time order, and the cleaning-step student onto keeping a step.
decisions.why: On planted tables their rules are weak (61%, 72%, 55%) while those students already hold the skill; a new student would learn the same thing from the same tables.

decisions.decision: generated_v3 from seeds 10,000 up, states written by solution_saved and cleaning into a scratch ledger.
decisions.why: The base students trained on generated_v2's seeds 0 to 2,399; an exam must hold no table they saw, and states built any other way than production's would test the wrong thing.

decisions.decision: Only modifier.groups sits its sealed exam.
decisions.why: On dev, with the gate's own function, time order equals the rule (no margin) and keeping a step turns 17.6% of the rule's right answers wrong (the gate allows 2%): reading those sealed sets would spend them on a known fail.

decisions.decision: tuning.accept's state carries the gain in units of the folds' spread, the candidates tried, the baseline's fold mean and spread, the family and the metric, in existing state fields.
decisions.why: The rule's 0.001 margin kept 22 of 149 tunings a fresh draw rejected; the old state held only the gain, rows and columns.

decisions.decision: No student for the file format, the label join key, noisy labels or review capacity.
decisions.why: Measured: the reader was right on 11 of 12 tricky files (the miss was a reader bug, fixed); the join key's misses need a product fix, not a whisper; noisy labels' state holds nothing a student could read; review capacity's truth is what the person says.

decisions.decision: The mapped students are not loaded in shadow and not listed as students.
decisions.why: Students that fail on dev would whisper false disagreements into the people's queue.

change: dclab_rnd/ledger/mapped.py (new), ledger/states.py (tuning_state), ledger/capture.py (the modifiers' split fields, tuning's state), decisions_gen.py (build_v3, keep_truth), decision_models_build.py (build_mapped), decision_gate_run.py (set v3), ledger/shadow.py (models_v3), students.py (generated_v3, models_v3, each student's own exam), archive.py, .gitignore, collector.py (the bar counts labelled decisions), tests.

findings.defect: Most planted points have no rule a student could beat.
findings.scenario: Planted tables: groups right 61%, time order 72%, a step kept 55%; nine points are settings, definitions or undecided.
findings.cause: The plan counted points, not rules to beat.
findings.fix: Map existing students onto the three weak ones; no student for the rest, each reason in the plan.

findings.defect: The tuning rule kept tunings a fresh draw rejected.
findings.scenario: 149 measured self-play labels: the rule right 82%, as often as always saying no.
findings.cause: A 0.001 margin on the best of several candidates on the same folds; the state held no spread.
findings.fix: tuning_state with the gain over the folds' spread and the candidates tried.

findings.defect: The register showed a passed student as not examined.
findings.scenario: column.semantic_role: DMG-014 (the real-table student, failed) overwrote DMG-004 (the register's student, passed): 'not examined (an earlier version failed)'.
findings.cause: verdicts kept only the latest exam per point.
findings.fix: Every exam kept; each student matched to the exam it sat.

findings.defect: The collector's run record called a point's homework met with no labels.
findings.fix: The bar counts decisions with a truth (a person's, measured or benchmark; never a model's), and their tables.

findings.defect: Tests pinned the old folder list and the old notebook read.
findings.scenario: test_label_queue's FOLDERS; test_labels's and test_studio's read lines.
findings.fix: The pinned folder list and read lines updated to the new ones.

findings.defect: The groups student's 100% came from counting columns, not from finding an entity.
findings.scenario: On every non-sealed v3 and v2 row, columns minus dates minus ids minus four above zero, or a repeat share above zero, equals the truth; adding one plain number column to a table with no entity flips the answer to yes.
findings.cause: benchgen2.split_table always draws three features and the outcome, so any further column that is neither a date nor an id is the planted entity; capture's split fields now pass the column count.
findings.fix: generated_v3 adds 0 to 5 plain columns drawn apart from the truth (decisions_gen.with_plain_columns); rebuilt before any sealed read and measured again.

findings.defect: The groups truth went against the product's own rule on tables with a time and an entity.
findings.scenario: 120 of 550 dev rows: the entity recurs over the whole period, where modifiers.detect deliberately asks the person; the label said yes and scored the ask as no.
findings.cause: The generator draws the entity apart from time.
findings.fix: Those tables are left out of the groups set, with the reason in its manifest.

findings.defect: The mapped student answered without its own fields.
findings.scenario: An older record {rows, has_time: True} got time order no; a table-wide step (duplicates) got keep no.
findings.cause: The base student reads a missing field as zero.
findings.fix: mapped.ready: every split field present, or a column step with the column's bands; otherwise it abstains.

findings.defect: The exam record did not say the student was mapped.
findings.scenario: DMG records copy the base student's family and trained set.
findings.cause: judge copied the card's training fields only.
findings.fix: The record keeps the card's chosen_by, which names the base student.

findings.defect: The plan's exam command would have spent all three sealed sets.
findings.scenario: --set v3 --yes without --points reads every point's sealed set.
findings.cause: The command in the plan named no point.

findings.defect: tuning_state could lose a whole record.
findings.scenario: A fold spread of 1e-16 made a ratio of 1e14, which the ledger refuses, and the tuning.accept record was dropped.
findings.cause: The ratio was taken for any spread above zero; '@' was kept in a code.
findings.fix: The ratio only above a spread of 1e-9; codes keep letters, digits and underscores.

findings.defect: A comment swallowed the candidates-tried field.
findings.scenario: tuning_state lost 'rounds' after the edit for R6.
findings.cause: An inline comment written before the next key on the same line.
findings.fix: The key on its own line.

findings.defect: The trained keep student's 100% read the dirty tables' layout.
findings.scenario: Dev: every wrong 'numbers' step is on a column of few values or of unique plain digits; a one-line rule on two bands scores 1,948 of 2,236, the student all.
findings.cause: benchgen v2's dirty tables plant no unique plain integers written as text that are numbers.
findings.fix: No exam; a generator package with each trap's counter-example proposed (benchgen v3 in dclab_core).
findings.test: the plan's table, measured in the session

measurements.name: mapped and trained students on the rebuilt generated_v3 dev
measurements.gate: decision_gate_v1's own verdict on dev rows (never sealed)
measurements.result: groups: mapped 42.8%, trained 82.6%, rule 80.9%; time order: 73.1% all three; keeping a step: mapped 86.9%, trained 100%, rule 74.6%
limits: the trained keep student's score rests on the dirty tables' layout

outcome: No new student sits an exam: on homework where a column count says nothing the mapped groups student fell to 42.8% (the rule 80.9%), and the one perfect trained student (keeping a cleaning step) read the dirty tables' layout. All sealed sets stay unread; the mapped students are not loaded in shadow. tuning.accept now records the evidence its student needs, and the register shows each student's own exam.
lessons: Count rules to beat, not points: a student is worth its homework only where the rule errs and the state holds evidence the rule ignores.
A register that keeps one exam per point hides the others: keep every exam and match each to the version that sat it.
A perfect score on planted homework is a question, not an answer: find the formula the generator leaves in the state before reading a sealed set.
risks: Planted homework scores mislead until the generator draws its layouts apart from every truth.
Time order needs a state that says how a date column behaves (its span, its order) before any student can beat the rule.
